items.title: Onaje Allan Gumbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001
items.q: Because he called me up one day and says, “I think you forgot who the leader of the band is, I don’t like your attitude, and I want my music back.

ctx.x: They can’t make it. Then all of a sudden it changes, he can come. But he can only come for one day. What? Then it changes, he can come for both days. So by the time Cannonball got to the campus we tried to question him about all this stuff. He said “well they told me to come for one day.” Okay. So I didn’t want to make a whole big thing or anything, but it’s something that kind of found a little spot in my brain, I found out about the attitude of the school. But moving ahead again, after college, the whole thing,…

and the Basic Black Band. Because Nat didn’t feel like doing all the road work, all the little stuff like the renting of the truck and all this kind of stuff. So he put that in our laps. But we got tired of it after a while. So that’s when he disbanded as a band, realizing he had to come back on board and take charge. Because we liked it for a while, and then we got kind of tired of it so we went to Nat and said listen, can we have a talk? So we had a band meeting. And that’s when he decided I’m going to…
He had a terrible accident, didn’t he?
